product_offering.core_offering: Moov provides a unified, open-source payment infrastructure platform that orchestrates the entire money movement lifecycle through a single REST API and one legal agreement. The core Moov Platform covers Accept (card and ACH acceptance, pay-by-bank, Tap to Pay on iPhone and Android), Store (Moov wallets, ledger, reporting), Send (instant payouts to bank accounts and debit cards via RTP, ACH, and push-to-card), and Spend (virtual card issuing with spend controls), and is sold to financial institutions, fintechs, and developers embedding payments into their own products.
product_offering.differentiator: Open source foundation allowing transparency and developer customization vs. closed proprietary systems. Single API integration covering all payment methods vs. multiple complex integrations. Modern architecture built from scratch without middleware vs. legacy pre-internet infrastructure. Real-time data visibility and warehouse sync vs. limited data visibility in traditional processors.
product_offering.functional_benefit: Instant tracking for faster, error-free payments; One API for all payment methods (cards, ACH, RTP, push-to-card); Transparent, synced data for full control and reconciliation; Modern reliability supporting today's transaction volumes; No middleware layer enabling direct integration control; Multiple payment rails accessible through single agreement (Visa Direct, Mastercard Move, RTP, FedNow capable)
product_offering.problem_solved: Fragmented payment infrastructure requiring multiple integrations; Legacy processors with slow batch processing and limited payment rails; Poor data visibility and reconciliation challenges; Pre-internet technology lacking modern reliability and scale; Complex compliance requirements for KYC/KYB
quantifiable_outcome: Over 200 credit unions and banks have adopted Rapid Transfers solution
Rapid Transfers live with 65 financial institutions, 170 more in implementation
Banno Digital Platform serves 1,000+ financial institutions and 15 million registered users
product_offering.product_overview: Moov offers a unified payment infrastructure platform built for technical teams, providing a single API integration to orchestrate the entire money movement lifecycle. The core Moov Platform supports four primary functions: Accept (card acceptance and pay-by-bank), Store (wallets and ledger), Send (instant payouts by bank and card), and Spend (virtual card issuing). The platform is modular, with additional products including Payment Links, Invoicing, Tap to Pay (iPhone and Android), Rapid Transfers, Tap2Local, Moov Drops (prebuilt UI components), Onboarding (streamlined merchant onboarding), Dashboard, and Data Sync. Built from open-source software, Moov targets financial institutions, lenders, construction companies, fundraising platforms, small businesses, and transportation/logistics companies through a B2B API-first approach.

product_and_service.description: Unified payment infrastructure platform that orchestrates the entire money movement lifecycle (Accept, Store, Send, Spend) through a single REST API integration and one legal agreement, providing visibility and control over the complete payment experience for financial institutions, fintechs, and vertical SaaS platforms.

profiles.name: Wade Arnold
profiles.overview: Founder and CEO of Moov, leading the company's mission to deliver open-source payment infrastructure for technical teams.
profiles.profile_commentary: Wade Arnold is the founder and CEO of Moov. As founder, he established the company in 2017/2018 in Cedar Falls, Iowa, with a vision to build payment infrastructure from scratch without middleware and on open-source software. Under his leadership, Moov raised approximately $77.5 million across multiple funding rounds (including a $45 million Series B in January 2023), grew to roughly 2,400 customers and $15.1 million ARR by 2024, and forged flagship strategic partnerships with Jack Henry (Rapid Transfers and Tap2Local solutions distributed through the Banno Digital Platform), Visa Direct, Mastercard Move, The Clearing House, Veridian Credit Union, and Lincoln Savings Bank. His founder-CEO positioning aligns with the company's identity as a developer-centric, open-source alternative to traditional payment processors.

profiles.name: Robert Smith
profiles.overview: Co-founder and President of Moov, responsible for company operations alongside CEO Wade Arnold.
profiles.profile_commentary: Robert Smith is a co-founder and serves as President of Moov. As co-founder, he helped establish Moov in 2017/2018 alongside Wade Arnold and continues to operate the business in the President role. His co-founder tenure spans the company's evolution from open-source payment infrastructure startup to a venture-backed fintech serving financial institutions (Jack Henry partnership reaching 1,000+ FIs and 15M+ users), vertical SaaS platforms (LoanPro, Trimble, Super Dispatch, Canopy, Valon), and SMBs (Tap2Local solution).

profiles.name: Josh Sadler
profiles.overview: VP of Product at Moov, leading product strategy and roadmap for the payment infrastructure platform.
profiles.profile_commentary: Josh Sadler serves as VP of Product at Moov, with responsibility for the platform's product strategy and roadmap. He leads product development across the unified Moov Platform (Accept, Store, Send, Spend), as well as recent product additions including Invoicing, Tap to Pay on iPhone and Android, Moov Drops prebuilt UI components, Data Sync, and the Rapid Transfers and Tap2Local solutions co-developed with Jack Henry.

profiles.name: Jared Jones
profiles.overview: Head of Ecosystem at Moov, responsible for partner and developer ecosystem development.
profiles.profile_commentary: Jared Jones serves as Head of Ecosystem at Moov, overseeing the company's partner and developer ecosystem. His role spans strategic partnerships (flagship Jack Henry relationship delivering Rapid Transfers and Tap2Local through the Banno Digital Platform), payment rail integrations (Visa Direct, Mastercard Move, The Clearing House RTP via Veridian Credit Union, Lincoln Savings Bank for card issuing), and developer community channels such as the Slack community, fintech_devcon events, and SDK distribution.

recent_move.description: Closed a $45 million Series B led by Commerce Ventures with participation from Andreessen Horowitz, Bain Capital Ventures, B3 Capital, Sorenson Ventures, and Visa.
Launched Rapid Transfers with Jack Henry as a flagship co-developed real-time A2A payment product on Visa Direct and Mastercard Move rails, live at 65 FIs with 170 in implementation.
Shipped Tap2Local with Jack Henry, enabling banks and credit unions to offer hardware-free tap-to-pay on iOS and Android to SMB customers, winning the 2026 FinTech Breakthrough Award.
Expanded product surface with Tap to Pay on Android, an Invoicing module with payment links and dunning, and ongoing API versioning through v2026.07.00 to capture SMB and creator workflows.

Deepened Jack Henry alliance by earning the 2026 FinTech Breakthrough "Small Business Payments Solution of the Year" award for the jointly developed Tap2Local product, validating the embedded distribution model.

Operationalized regulated bank-institution partnerships with Veridian Credit Union (RTP FI Partner) and Lincoln Savings Bank (card-issuing Issuer) to support card issuing and RTP rails within the unified platform.

expansion_highlight.description: Tap2Local and Rapid Transfers co-developed with Jack Henry are being rolled out across 65 live FIs with 170 in implementation, signaling aggressive channel-led expansion into the community bank and credit union segment.
Tap to Pay on iPhone and Tap to Pay on Android launched in 2024, opening a hardware-free in-person acceptance vertical for SMBs that historically required separate terminal hardware vendors.

API version roadmap extending through v2026.07.00, ongoing feature additions (Invoicing, Payment Links, Data Sync), and a published product roadmap indicate sustained platform investment and broadening surface area for cross-sell.

Moov currently restricts service to US-domiciled businesses ("International markets (non-US businesses are not currently supported)"), making cross-border enablement a natural upside lever once regulatory and FI partnerships are secured.

New vertical use cases (construction, fundraising, loan servicing, transportation) beyond the core digital-banking segment indicate horizontal SaaS-style expansion across verticalized payment workflows.
Hiring of a VP of Product and Head of Ecosystem alongside 101–250 employee scale suggests organizational buildout to support a multi-product, partner-led GTM motion.
